items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mingus was with the band then... Tony, rather, always wanted to play in Ellington’s band... So we finally got that going.

ctx.x: . . . Tony Scott. They started talking about various and sundry things, like you do on a bus trip, particularly with no ladies on it, and it got deeply ensconced in sex. Tony went on to use a term that is used – in caucasian vernacular, it has a slightly different meaning than when we use it in the ghetto vernacular. He kept using this word . . .
